instructions: Read the passage and choose one answer for each question.
passage:
Lila and her cousin Ben want to move closer to their language class. They visit two places in the same neighborhood on Tuesday. The first apartment is on Oak Street, and the second is on Elm Street. Lila has written the address of each one in her notebook. She wants to compare the rooms and the monthly costs before making a decision.

The Oak apartment has a monthly rent of 720 pounds. Its bedroom is smaller than the one on Elm Street, but its kitchen is larger. The bathroom is private, and the living room feels spacious to both visitors. There is enough space for Ben's desk, and the window looks out onto a small garden. Lila likes the light, while Ben notices that the ceiling is higher than the ceiling in his current room.

The landlord says that the next tenant can use the furniture included in the apartment: a table, two chairs and a bed. Lila checks the floor beside the table and photographs a mark on the wall. She also sees a small leak near the bathroom door. The landlord says a repair is planned before the next tenant moves in. Lila writes this down and asks for the planned work to be included in their written agreement. She does not assume that a spoken promise is the same as completed work.

Ben asks how the heating works and whether electricity and gas are included. The landlord shows them an example bill and says the electricity charge is separate from the rent. The gas charge is also separate. Ben notes both points so that the family can ask about the likely costs later. They do not assume that rent covers every household expense.

The landlord shows Lila a draft contract for a twelve-month lease. The proposed deposit is 400 pounds. Lila wants to read the document carefully before signing and ask what happens if existing damage appears in the photographs. She and Ben take a copy home rather than agreeing at the door. The details in this fictional offer are specific to this apartment.

The Elm apartment costs 760 pounds each month. It is as quiet as the Oak apartment, but the kitchen is not as large. Its gate looks secure, although Lila knows that a quick look cannot guarantee safety. On the bus home, Ben says that Oak is better for his desk but that the leak and the separate bills need answers. Lila agrees. They will compare the notes, ask their questions and then decide together.
